direction: February listens to ordinary traces: touch held by a wall, a small offering at the waterline, and grass beside a brook. Close material study, sparse water wash and low living landscape vary density and medium. The mythic ghazal and the historical comparison remain text-led.

items.title: Touch held in the wall
items.rationale: The beloved asks for a keepsake, but years of touch already remain in the house. A close, ordinary door jamb and winter sunlight imply shared life without a staged couple or sentimental objects.

review.notes: Normal-size review passes: cropped door and jamb connect coherently to plaster and floor; side sunlight falls across the wall and floor with plausible continuity. Ordinary rubbed wood and sparse wall texture preserve the memory of touch without staged keepsakes or people. Some low-edge wear is visible but does not become a ruin. Warm gouache material study and broad quiet wall distinguish it from the previous window-creeper scene.

items.alt: Winter sunlight crosses a pale wall beside a gently worn wooden doorway.

items.title: What the tide brings
items.rationale: The speaker offers broken pieces of ego, blue feathers, petals and a shared poem toward the beloved’s shore. A single feather at a quiet waterline carries the uncertain offering; leave the ending unresolved rather than assemble all the objects.

review.notes: Normal-size review passes: one slate-blue feather has a single continuous shaft and uneven barbs, rests on damp sand, and touches the shallow arriving ripple at its quill. Water strokes remain broken and varied rather than geometric. Restrained light, pale upper space and an unresolved offering retain the poem’s loneliness without staging every named object. Painted interpretation, no species or location claim.

items.alt: A slate-blue feather rests where a shallow ripple reaches wet sand.

items.title: A blade beside the brook
items.rationale: Poetry emerges through grass and water without being forced as a duty. A few small grass shoots at a brook’s edge keep attention with the lesser and ordinary, leaving the poem’s many transformations to the reader.

review.notes: Normal-size review passes: grass emerges from a supported earth bank with uneven lengths and bends, water divides around the partly submerged main stone, and shallow foreground stones remain subordinate. Additional peripheral stones are physically consistent with the brook and do not change its emotional anchor. Broken paint edges and pale upper water preserve breathing room. No fantastical transformations or collected poem nouns; a painted moment of ordinary attention.

items.alt: Uneven green grass grows from a low earth bank beside a softly flowing brook.

text_led.rationale: The ghazal moves through intimate dialogue and layered myth; leave those transformations in language rather than reduce them to a crowded deity tableau.
The comparison of Dharama and Socrates is an argument about sacrifice and authority. Preserve it as text without inventing a historical likeness, suicide scene or architectural reconstruction.
